content:
I'd like to announce QuadraticIterates, a formalzation of the contents of my first published paper (Galois groups over Q of some iterated polynomials, Arch. Math. 59, 239-244 (1992), DOI:  10.1007/BF01197321). The main result is that for many integers aaa, the Galois groups over Q\mathbb QQ of all iterates of x2+ax^2 + ax2+a are as large as possible.

A first formalization was obtained by Logos Research's system while I was at the FLT workshop in London earlier this year. This first formalization (or, rather, a somewhat improved version that was made available to me by Logos Research) then formed the basis of an effort over several weeks to turn it into code that gets close to Mathlib quality. This was achieved by letting Claude (mostly Fable, also Opus) work on the code in a tight feedback loop. The last round was done with Fable 5.1 and has improved code quality significantly in my assessment. The current version is about 4000 lines total (~2500 of which are actual Lean code, i.e., not counting comments and empty lines), so it is not too overwhelming to look at.

The repo has a formalization.yaml file and a comparator setup for the main results. It also follows the template of containing a Mathlib subfolder that contains material that (Claude thinks) should be upstreamable to Mathlib. One point of note here is the development of a general theory of multiquadratic field extensions.

Comments are welcome (in particular regarding code quality)!

As an indication of what the last round of code improvement did, here is a table comparing proof lengths before and after (produced by Claude, of course):

Proof lengths: 2026-08-30 vs 2026-09-05

Proof length = number of lines from the := to the end of the declaration (signature excluded),
for all theorems and lemmas under QuadraticIterates/ (definitions excluded). Baseline: the
initial commit cd6e871 (2026-08-30); current: aa54510 (2026-09-05).

2026-08-30 2026-09-05 change
theorems and lemmas 264 304 +40
total proof lines 2676 1409 −47 %
mean / median 10.1 / 6 4.6 / 3

I should mention that "proof length at most 20 lines" is a "soft" rule in the guidelines I give Claude.
